title: Fresno's airport has 'tremendous opportunity' to continue expanding, new boss says - NewsBreak
text:
By Christian Valdez No media credit provided. ,
2 hours ago
FRESNO, Calif. ( KSEE/KGPE ) – Fresno Yosemite International Airport’s new aviation director, Mark Thorpe, was announced on Wednesday, and he plans to expand its reach.
Mark Thorpe has 27 years of commercial aviation experience, according to the city. Thorpe has been an executive at Los Angeles International Airport, Dallas/Fort Worth International Airport, and Ontario International Airport. These are some of the largest airports in North America.
“As Fresno Yosemite International Airport continues to grow and evolve, I am confident he is the right leader to guide the airport into its next chapter,” said City Manager Georgeanne White.
Fresno Yosemite completed its biggest expansion last December with the addition of the new terminal. Thorpe’s vast experience can be vital for the growing airport.
“There is a tremendous opportunity for Fresno Airport to continue expanding connectivity throughout the United States, Mexico, Canada, and Central America,” Thorpe said.
Fresno Yosemite International Airport provides flights to three cities in Mexico and does not fly directly to Canada. Thorpe has helped secure service to 32 new domestic and international destinations while working in Los Angeles and Ontario. Thorpe’s ability to initiate expansion in the past can help here in Fresno.
Thorpe also plans to make improvements to concessions and amenities within the airport to improve the customer experience, according to the city.
Thorpe will be overseeing the operation and direction of Fresno International Airport and Fresno Chandler Executive Airport, according to the city. Expansion may be in the near future under Thorpe’s direction.
